dataset_metadata.dataset_name: Official Meal Delivery Demand Benchmark Dataset
dataset_metadata.data_distinction_note: OFFICIAL REFERENCE DATASET ONLY: These benchmarks reflect the 456,548-record historical meal delivery fulfillment dataset. They DO NOT represent KitchenVerse real customer order history or live kitchen profiles.

validation_protocol.strategy: Strict Chronological Split (No Shuffling, No Future Leakage)
leakage_prevention: Strict time-based split: weeks 1-116 strictly precede test weeks 117-145
Label encoders and standard scalers fit exclusively on training data (weeks 1-116)
Unseen test categories mapped safely to default class
Time-series baseline computes predictions strictly using history prior to each forecasted week
No target encoding or future target aggregation applied across time boundary

metrics_defined.mae: Mean Absolute Error — average raw order forecast deviation (lower is better)
metrics_defined.rmse: Root Mean Squared Error — penalizes large order variance spikes (lower is better)
metrics_defined.r2: Coefficient of Determination — variance of demand explained (higher is better)
metrics_defined.mape_pct: Safe Mean Absolute Percentage Error — relative error with zero/near-zero clipping (lower is better)

XGBoost Regressor.description: Histogram-optimized gradient boosted ensemble with subsampling and feature fractioning.

Random Forest Regressor.description: Bootstrap aggregated ensemble of 100 deep regression trees with leaf regularization.

Linear Regression.description: L2-regularized linear model with strictly train-fitted standard scaling and one-hot encoding.

hyperparameters.strategy: Rolling moving average per (center_id, meal_id) series with sequential history update
hyperparameters.fallback: Expanding historical pair mean -> Center mean -> Global training mean

Time-Series Baseline.description: Chronological rolling moving average per fulfillment-meal series strictly using prior historical weeks without future leakage.

Gradient Boosting (Reference).description: Original KitchenVerse production reference model trained with robust Huber loss on order demand.

best_model.selection_rationale: Random Forest Regressor achieved the best balanced performance across all evaluated metrics: MAE of 90.009, RMSE of 191.098, R² of 0.7262, and MAPE of 68.90%.

limitations: Reference dataset covers fulfillment centers and aggregated weekly orders, not sub-hourly kitchen rush windows.
Historical promotions and prices in the reference dataset do not model individual dynamic kitchen pricing in real-time.
Linear models struggle with complex non-linear promotional and meal-center interaction effects.
Time-series baseline without exogenous promotional features lags behind gradient-boosted trees during sudden marketing campaigns.
